q: What should I wear ice skating?
a: Warm, flexible layers, gloves and one pair of thin-to-medium socks. Skip jeans that soak through when you fall, and bring a helmet for young children. Our guide on what to wear covers indoor and outdoor rinks.

q: Is outdoor pond ice safe to skate on?
a: Natural ice is never guaranteed safe, and its thickness can vary a lot across one pond. A supervised, maintained rink is the safer choice. If you do skate on natural ice, follow your state natural resources agency's guidance and never go alone.

q: A rink is missing or its details are wrong. How do I fix it?
a: Email us from the contact page with the rink's name and what needs to change. Corrections and additions are free, and rink owners can ask us to update or remove a listing at any time.
